title: Instructions
section: 29. Capstone Project - Use a Public API
summary: Brief for the Section 29 capstone: build an Express + Axios + EJS website around a public API of the learner's choice, with error handling, comments, a README and a GitHub push. The lecture page body did not render in the browser, so this note is based on the reference repo's section README, which holds the brief.

concepts.heading: Capstone brief
points: Build a site on Node/Express that uses Axios to call a public API picked from the course's public-api-lists repo (or any other). Show the retrieved data in a friendly way.
Goals: practise integrating public APIs, server-side Express, client-server communication with Axios, and handling and presenting API data.

Example ideas: a joke based on the user's name (JokeAPI), a will-it-rain-tomorrow checker (OpenWeatherMap), a crypto price lookup, a random cocktail recipe with images (CocktailDB), a sunscreen-today helper (Open UV). Bonus for choosing an unusual API; if a chosen API turns out unusable, switch to another.

concepts.heading: Requirements checklist
points: API choice: prefer one that needs no authentication and has CORS enabled.
Planning: research the API's features, the data it returns and how the app will use it before coding.
Setup: new Node project with Express, Axios and EJS, organised into a sensible directory structure (index.js, views, public).
Integration: implement at least one GET endpoint that sends Axios requests to the API and handles the responses.
Presentation: render data with EJS, HTML and CSS so it reads well for a user.
Error handling: handle failures in the app and in API calls; log errors and show user-relevant messages where useful.
Documentation: comment the code to explain the logic.
Sharing: commit and push to GitHub, and include a README explaining how to install and start (npm i, then nodemon index.js).

concepts.heading: Recommended resources
points: Express getting-started guide, Node docs, Axios docs, the public API list repo, and RapidAPI's list of free APIs.

task.name: Section 29 capstone: use a public API
task.starting_point: Empty project; reference repo has two example solutions (29.01 Get a Joke, 29.02 Know The Rain) each with index.js, views/index.ejs and package.json.
task.goal: Ship a small Express/Axios/EJS app that fetches and displays data from a public API, with error handling, comments, a README and a GitHub repo.
steps: Browse the public API list and pick an API (no auth, CORS enabled preferred).
Read its docs and plan routes, inputs and displayed fields.
npm init, install express, axios and ejs; create index.js, views/ and public/.
Add at least one GET route that calls the API with Axios (async/await in try/catch).
Render the data via an EJS template with CSS.
Add error handling and code comments.
Write a README with run instructions and push to GitHub; optionally share in the Q&A.
task.expected_result: A working site that displays live API data in a readable layout and fails gracefully.
task.reference_repo_path: Section 29 - Capstone Project - Use a Public API/

pitfalls: Picking an API that requires keys or lacks CORS/docs adds friction.
Hard-coding API keys in code pushed to GitHub.
Reference examples set res.status(500) without sending a body, leaving the request hanging.
Skipping the README or comments, which are explicit requirements.
